requirements.quote: Every payment operation request (authorize, capture, refund or reversal) must carry an idempotency key, and a repeated key must return the original result without repeating the operation.
Refunds and reversals above 1,000 EUR must be approved by a second person, and the person who requested the operation must not be able to approve it.
Payment amounts and currencies should be protected against tampering in a manner appropriate to the risk.
Every query on merchant data must be filtered by the tenant identifier taken from the authenticated token and never from a request parameter.
Tenant data in shared storage should be separated by row-level security or by tenant-specific encryption keys.
Uploaded files must not exceed 10 MB, and their type must be checked against an allowed list on the content of the file, not on its name.
Uploaded files must be scanned for malware before any other user or service can open them.
Mobile apps must pin the public key or the certificate of the Meridian Pay API and must refuse connections that fail the check.
Mobile apps must keep tokens and keys only in the secure storage of the operating system and never in preferences or in files.
Alerts about repeated failed logins, privilege changes and access to card data must reach the on-call engineer within 15 minutes.
Services must maintain appropriate procedures for responding to security incidents.
Every third-party SDK or library must be approved before its first use, and the list of approved components must be reviewed every six months.
Third-party scripts must not be loaded into web pages that handle card data or credentials.
Databases must have point-in-time recovery enabled with at least seven days of retention.
The recovery time objective of a critical service must not exceed 4 hours, and it must be proven by a failover exercise at least once a year.
For batch services a recovery time objective of up to 24 hours is acceptable.
